added: This section covers pacing (the waits that hold a run to wall-clock time).
Its parts are the invariant with the wall-clock map, the wait, the diagnostics, and where staging and concurrency live.
#### The invariant and the wall-clock map
(the records of each frame's drained inputs)
(the atomic surface carrying pause, pace and stop)
Here $p$ is the pace and $\tau$ is wall-clock time.
The anchor pair $(t_{\mathrm{anchor}}, \tau_{\mathrm{anchor}})$ is the sim time and wall-clock time at the most recent anchor.
